page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the left margin (two references beside the lines). The page number and running head are at the top. Below the text, at the right, is the catchword "doni-".

main_text.p: violetur. Ut eâ in re, non minus delinquat, quam si ipsi sibi violentas manus intulisset. Nam qui vitam negligit, eamque suâ culpâ amittit, idem est, ac si seipsum occidisset. Probatur. 3. Quia quisque regulariter plus tenetur, sibi, suaeque vitae providere, quam vitae alterius; saltem aequè sibi prospicere tenetur, quam proximo; idque ex mandato Christi; Ephes. cap. 5. v.29.Matth. c. 22. v.39.proximum diliges, sicut teipsum. Verum si patiatur se potius occidi, quâ ut iniquum interficiat invalorem[?], non ita sibi consulit; atque quidem proximo consulere debuisset.

Licebit enim in gratiâ proximi ab adversario oppressi, actum moderatæ tutelæ exercere, ne occidatur, ut id æque liceat, si non magis, ad evitandam sui occisionem. Vnde ferunt, Lutherum, interrogatum aliquando, num à prae-

page.notes: The first left-margin note "Ephes. cap. 5. v.29." (printed "Ephef. cap. 5. v.29.") and the second "Matth. c. 22. v.39." are placed where their reference marks stand in the text. The word "invalorem" is doubtful: the letters are unclear in the scan and could be "invasorem"; it is marked [?]. Small marks ("•", ",") in the left margin near the lines are scan dirt or stray marks and are not transcribed. The catchword "doni-" is the start of the next page's first word. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.
